title: Dynamic Inventory Synchronization for Global Retail
business: A global retail platform managing real-time stock levels across multiple regional warehouses.
problem: The system suffers from stale inventory data where customers purchase items that are already out of stock because the application layer continues to serve cached, outdated availability results.
solution: Implementing an event-driven cache invalidation strategy where the inventory database triggers a purge command to the cache layer immediately upon a successful transaction, ensuring subsequent requests fetch the current state.
steps: Configure a database trigger on the inventory table to detect write operations.
Develop a listener service that receives notification of inventory changes.
Execute a cache purge command targeting the specific product ID key.
Verify the cache miss on the next read request to force a database refresh.
outcome: Customers receive accurate, real-time availability information, significantly reducing order cancellations due to overselling.
limitation: The primary limitation is the 'cache stampede' risk, where simultaneous requests for an invalidated key overwhelm the database; this can be checked by monitoring the latency spikes during high-concurrency periods following an invalidation event.

options: To prevent customers from purchasing items that are already out of stock.
To increase the total storage capacity of the database.
To reduce the number of users accessing the website.
To permanently delete product records from the database.
questions.explanation: The scenario identifies that stale cached data leads to overselling, which invalidation resolves.

questions.question: In Dynamic Inventory Synchronization for Global Retail, what is a key limitation of the proposed invalidation strategy?
options: The system becomes too fast for the database to handle.
The risk of a cache stampede during high-concurrency periods.
The database trigger will automatically delete all product data.
The application will stop serving requests entirely.
